statement: A curve is given parametrically by $x=t^{2}$, $y=t^{3}$. (i) Find $\frac{dy}{dx}$ in terms of $t$. (ii) Find the equation of the tangent at $t=2$. (iii) Show that this tangent meets the curve again at $t=-1$.
solution: (i) $\frac{dx}{dt}=2t$, $\frac{dy}{dt}=3t^{2}$, so $\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{3t^{2}}{2t}=\frac{3t}{2}$ ($t\neq0$). (ii) At $t=2$: point $(4,8)$, slope $3$. Tangent: $y-8=3(x-4)$, i.e. $y=3x-4$. (iii) On the curve $y=t^{3},x=t^{2}$; substitute: $t^{3}=3t^{2}-4\Rightarrow t^{3}-3t^{2}+4=0$. $t=2$ is a root: factor $(t-2)^{2}(t+1)=0$. The other intersection is at $t=-1$, point $(1,-1)$, which lies on $y=3x-4$ since $3(1)-4=-1$.
hints: Substitute the parametric form into the tangent line.
